mainTopic: Suspecting a woman of lying to harm a relative, and how conflicting testimonies about a husband's death are weighed (one against two, majority of voices, wives who contradict each other)
overview: The גמרא tries to answer an open question: is a woman suspected of lying to harm a relative, even one she is not yet related to? It brings a ברייתא in which a daughter-in-law's report that her husband and father-in-law died does not let her mother-in-law remarry, because she might be lying to get rid of her. The proof is rejected, because a daughter-in-law has already suffered from her mother-in-law. Next comes a משנה about witnesses who disagree over whether a husband died: one against one, one against two, and two against one. Using עולא's rule that one believed witness counts as two, the גמרא explains that once she was permitted to remarry, a single later witness cannot cancel that permission. It then explains the other cases using רבי נחמיה's rule of following the majority of voices, even of people normally unfit to testify, and it shows this works both to forbid and to permit. A new משנה follows about two wives who disagree: one says he died and one says he did not, or one says he died and one says he was killed, where רבי מאיר argues with רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון. The amud ends as the משנה begins a case of one witness against one, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A proof is brought from a daughter-in-law's testimony
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: a woman who says her husband died and then her father-in-law died may remarry and collect her כתובה, but her mother-in-law may not remarry based on her word.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If she said, "My husband died, and afterward my father-in-law died," she may marry and collect her כתובה, but her mother-in-law is forbidden to remarry.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the open question. This step only quotes the source; the next step explains why it might prove something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The woman is believed about her own husband, so she may remarry and collect her כתובה. Her testimony does not help her mother-in-law, who stays forbidden to remarry. The גמרא will now ask why her word is not trusted for the mother-in-law.

keyTerms.meaning: The marriage contract money owed to a wife when the marriage ends

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If she said: "My husband died
and afterward my father-in-law died"
she may marry and collect her marriage contract,
and her mother-in-law is forbidden to remarry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a proof attempt for the question raised before this section.
steps.raayaObject: The open question of whether a woman is suspected of lying to harm a relative, even when the relationship has not formed yet
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a daughter-in-law's testimony does not permit her mother-in-law to remarry

steps.title: Why the mother-in-law is forbidden: the daughter-in-law wants to get rid of her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the daughter-in-law is suspected of making up the deaths so that her mother-in-law remarries and is out of her life.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason her mother-in-law is forbidden? Is it not because we say that maybe her husband did not die and her father-in-law did not die, and she said this only to ruin her mother-in-law? She thinks: Later on, my mother-in-law will not come and trouble me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind the ברייתא to show how it answers the open question. It says the daughter-in-law may be lying to get her mother-in-law out of the picture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the mother-in-law remarries and her husband turns out to be alive, she can never go back to him. So the daughter-in-law would never have to deal with her again. The proof says: we suspect a woman of lying to harm a relative even in a way that affects the future.

keyTerms.meaning: To ruin her, to cause her harm

steps.confusionAlert: The daughter-in-law is still believed about her OWN husband's death. She is suspected only regarding her mother-in-law.

phrases.english: What is the reason her mother-in-law is forbidden?
Is it not because we say:
maybe her husband did not die,
and her father-in-law did not die,
and the reason she says this
is that she intends to ruin her mother-in-law,
She reasons: Later on,
she will not come and trouble me.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some don't. Either way, she means her mother-in-law won't be around to bother her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the ברייתא from step 1 to turn it into a proof.
steps.raayaObject: The open question about suspecting a woman of lying to harm a relative
steps.raayaSupportSource: The reasoning behind the ברייתא: the daughter-in-law lies so her mother-in-law will be out of her life later

steps.title: The proof is rejected: she has already suffered from her mother-in-law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a daughter-in-law is different, because she has already felt pain from her mother-in-law, so there is a real reason to suspect her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it is different there, because she has already felt pain from her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The case of the daughter-in-law may be special and may not answer the open question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter-in-law has a real history of suffering from her mother-in-law, so she has a motive to lie. In a relationship that has not started yet, there is no such history. So the ברייתא cannot settle the question.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא about the חמותה does not prove the open question. The daughter-in-law is suspected because she has already suffered, and that may not apply to a relationship that has not formed yet.

phrases.english: Perhaps it is different there,
because she has already felt pain from her.
phrases.notes: "Her" here is the mother-in-law, who has already caused the daughter-in-law suffering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof built in steps 1 and 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the ברייתא as proof for the open question
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא involves a relationship where pain has already been felt, unlike a relationship that has not begun

steps.title: One witness against one after she remarried: she stays married
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה rules that if she remarried based on one witness, a single later witness who says the husband is alive does not force her to leave.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If one witness says "he died" and she married, and then one came and said "he did not die," she does not have to leave.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins about witnesses who disagree on whether the husband died. The first case is one witness against one witness after she has already remarried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One witness is enough to let a woman remarry. Once she has remarried, a single opposing witness is not strong enough to undo it, so she stays with her new husband.

keyTerms.meaning: She does not leave (her new husband)

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If one witness says "he died," and she married,
and one other witness came and said "he did not die,"
she does not have to leave.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, separate from the earlier discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One witness against one after she remarried: she stays with her new husband.

steps.title: One witness against two: she must leave
steps.stepSummary: If one witness says the husband died but two say he is alive, she must leave her new husband even if she already remarried.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one witness says "he died" and two say "he did not die," even though she already married, she must leave.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second case. Now two witnesses oppose the single witness.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses are a full testimony (עדות גמורה) and outweigh one witness. So even after she remarried, the marriage must end.

phrases.english: If one witness says "he died,"
and two say "he did not die,"
even though she married, she must leave.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֵד אוֹמֵר מֵת וּשְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים לֹא מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case of the משנה: two witnesses instead of one oppose the first witness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two witnesses saying he is alive outweigh one who says he died; she must leave even after remarrying.

steps.title: Two witnesses against one: she may remarry
steps.stepSummary: If two witnesses say the husband died and one says he is alive, she may remarry even if she has not yet done so.
steps.simpleTranslation: If two say "he died" and one witness says "he did not die," even though she has not yet married, she may marry.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third case, the reverse of the second. Two witnesses say he died and only one disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two witnesses outweigh one, so their testimony stands. She may remarry from the start; she does not need to have already remarried for this to work.

keyTerms.meaning: That she has not yet married

steps.whatToRemember: Two witnesses beat one. For one witness against one, step 8 explains that once בית דין permitted her based on the first witness, she may marry even before the wedding.

phrases.english: If two say "he died,"
and one witness says "he did not die,"

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נִשֵּׂאת, תִּנָּשֵׂא.
phrases.english: even though she has not married, she may marry.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַיִם אוֹמְרִים מֵת וְעֵד אוֹמֵר לֹא מֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third case of the משנה, the reverse of step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two witnesses saying he died outweigh one who says he is alive; she may remarry even before she has done so.

steps.title: Why only if she already remarried?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads the משנה as saying that the single later witness fails only because she already remarried. It then challenges this with עולא's rule that one believed witness counts as two.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: The reason she stays married is that she already married. So if she had not yet married, she may not marry. But didn't עולא say: wherever the Torah believes one witness, it is as if there are two here, and the words of one witness have no weight against two?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא first draws an inference from the משנה: she keeps her new marriage only because she already remarried. It then attacks that inference using a rule of עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא holds that when the Torah believes one witness, as with a missing husband, that witness counts like two. If so, the later single witness is just one person against 'two', and he should be ignored completely. She should be allowed to marry even if she has not married yet, so why does the משנה make it depend on her already being married?

keyTerms.meaning: The reason; the גמרא is pointing to what the ruling depends on
But if; introduces the opposite case that we infer

keyTerms.term: אֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם
keyTerms.meaning: The words of one witness have no weight against two

steps.confusionAlert: The 'two' in עולא's rule is not two real people. It is one witness whom the Torah treats as strong as two.
steps.whyThisMatters: עולא's rule, that one believed witness counts as two, drives both questions in this part of the sugya.

phrases.english: GEMARA
The reason is that she married
phrases.notes: This goes back to the משנה in step 4: one witness said he died, she remarried, then one said he is alive.

phrases.english: but if she did not marry
she may not marry
But didn't עולא say

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד
phrases.english: wherever the Torah believed one witness
it is as if there are two here

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם
phrases.english: and the words of one have no weight against two

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּנִשֵּׂאת, הָא לֹא נִשֵּׂאת — לֹא תִּנָּשֵׂא. וְהָאָמַר עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the גמרא's discussion of the משנה rulings from steps 4 through 6, starting with step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a single contradicting witness blocks remarriage if she has not yet married
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under עולא's rule, the first witness counts as two, so one later witness cannot outweigh him even before she marries.

steps.title: The משנה means she may even marry from the start
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the משנה: once she was permitted based on one witness, a later single witness does not take away that permission, even if she has not married yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what the משנה means: one witness says 'He died,' and they permitted her to marry. Then another one came and said 'He did not die.' She does not lose her first permission.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by explaining the משנה differently. 'Married' in the משנה really means she was given permission to marry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The deciding moment is when בית דין permitted her, not the wedding itself. Once permission was given based on the first witness, who counts as two, a later single witness cannot cancel it. This fits עולא's rule exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; the גמרא rereads the earlier text
And they permitted her to marry

steps.whatToRemember: Once she was permitted to remarry based on one witness, a single later witness who contradicts him cannot cancel that permission, even before she marries.

phrases.english: This is what it means
one witness says "He died"
and they permitted her to marry
and one came and said "He did not die"
she does not leave her first permission
phrases.notes: Here 'does not leave' means she keeps her permission and may go ahead and marry. It does not mean leaving a husband.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from עולא in step 7.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה protects her only if she has already married.
steps.terutzMaskana: The permission itself protects her, so she may marry even if she has not done so yet.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that two beat one?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה needs to say that two witnesses saying 'alive' outweigh one saying 'dead'. That seems obvious.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said that if one witness says 'He died' and two say he is alive, she must leave. But that is obvious, since the words of one have no weight against two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns to the next ruling of the משנה (step 5) and asks why it needs to be taught at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once two real witnesses testify against him, the single first witness is just one voice against two, and as the גמרא says, the words of one have no weight against two. So the ruling that she must leave seems too simple to need saying.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; asks why the text needs to say this

phrases.english: A witness says "He died"
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה's case from step 5: one says he died, but two say he is alive.

phrases.english: It is obvious

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין דְּבָרָיו שֶׁל אֶחָד בִּמְקוֹם שְׁנַיִם
phrases.english: since the words of one have no weight against two

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the first ruling of the משנה to the second ruling (step 5).
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that two witnesses for 'alive' make her leave
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two witnesses clearly outweigh one, so the משנה seems to be teaching something we already know.

steps.title: The two are disqualified witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about two people who normally cannot testify, and it follows רבי נחמיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for the case of people disqualified from giving testimony, and it follows the view of רבי נחמיה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the new point of the משנה: the two who say 'alive' are people normally disqualified as witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, people disqualified from testimony could not outweigh a valid witness. The משנה teaches that here their two voices still beat the one valid witness. This only works according to רבי נחמיה, whose source comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: No, it is needed (for a special case)

phrases.english: No, it is needed
for people disqualified from testimony
phrases.notes: He means the two who say he is alive are the disqualified ones, like women.

phrases.english: and in line with רבי נחמיה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'it is obvious' question from step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about two valid witnesses, so it says nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even two disqualified witnesses outweigh the one valid witness.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה: follow the majority of voices
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the ברייתא of רבי נחמיה: wherever one witness is believed, follow the majority of voices, so two women against one man count like two men against one man.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי נחמיה says, wherever the Torah believed one witness, follow the majority of opinions. They treated two women against one man like two men against one man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the source for רבי נחמיה's view, which supports the answer in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When one witness is believed, the testimony is counted by number of voices, not by who is a valid witness. So two women, who are normally disqualified, outweigh one valid man. This is exactly the case the משנה needed to teach.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי נחמיה, when one witness is believed we count voices. Two disqualified witnesses, like two women, outweigh one valid witness.

phrases.english: As it is taught: רבי נחמיה says

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד
phrases.english: wherever the Torah believed one witness
follow the majority of opinions
and they made two women against one man
like two men against one man

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the ברייתא behind the reference to רבי נחמיה in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That two disqualified witnesses can outweigh one valid witness in the case of a missing husband

steps.title: A first qualified witness cannot be outweighed by women
steps.stepSummary: Another approach: if a qualified witness testified first, even a hundred women count only as one witness. The case under discussion is one where a woman testified first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: whenever one qualified witness came first, even a hundred women who disagree count only as one witness. So our case must be one where a woman came first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second answer to the 'it is obvious' question of step 9. It explains the משנה's case as one where a woman, not a qualified man, testified first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A qualified witness who came first has the full strength of two witnesses. A crowd of women cannot overturn him. Because of this, the 'majority' case must be one where the first testimony also came from a woman.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you wish, say: introduces another possible answer
One witness who is fully fit to testify
They are treated like a single witness

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
Anywhere that there came
one qualified witness at the start
phrases.notes: He means a witness who first testified that the husband died, and she was permitted based on him.

phrases.english: even a hundred women
are like one witness.
Rather, it is a case such as
where a woman came at the start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the 'it is obvious' question of step 9, as an alternative to the answer in steps 10 and 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two women could outweigh one qualified man who testified first.
steps.terutzMaskana: A qualified witness who testified first cannot be outweighed even by many women. The majority case applies only when a woman testified first.

steps.title: Rewording רבי נחמיה's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה's ברייתא is reworded: two women against one woman are like two men against one man. Two women against one man, however, are only half against half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Fix רבי נחמיה's teaching like this: wherever the Torah believes one witness, follow the majority. Two women against one woman are like two men against one man. But two women against one man are equal, half and half.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adjusts the wording of the ברייתא from step 11 so that it matches the approach just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the ברייתא said two women against one man work like a majority. Now it says the majority rule works only for two women against one woman. Against one qualified man, two women only tie him, because he counts as two.

keyTerms.meaning: Half and half, an even tie

steps.whatToRemember: One qualified man counts as two. So two women against him are a tie, not a majority. Only women against women follow the majority.

phrases.english: And fix the teaching of רבי נחמיה like this:
רבי נחמיה says:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל מָקוֹם שֶׁהֶאֱמִינָה תּוֹרָה עֵד אֶחָד
phrases.english: Wherever the Torah believed one witness,
follow the majority of opinions,
and they made two women against one woman
like two men against one man.
But two women against one man
are like half and half.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rewords the ברייתא so that it fits the approach of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא says two women outweigh one man.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא really says two women outweigh one woman. Against one man, it is a tie.

steps.title: Why does the משנה need the 'two say dead' case?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's next case, two say he died and one says he did not, seems to teach nothing new. It looks the same as the case before it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'Two say he died, and one says he did not.' What is it teaching us? If it means people unfit to testify, following רבי נחמיה's majority rule, then this is the same as the earlier case!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks why it is needed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier case (two say alive, one says dead) was already explained as unfit witnesses following the majority. This new case is just the reverse. So it seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: People who are normally unfit to testify
This is the same as that

phrases.english: 'Two say: He died,' etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the line: one says he did not die, and even if she has not married yet, she may marry.

phrases.english: What is it teaching us?
If it is about people unfit to testify,
and it follows רבי נחמיה,
who goes after the majority of opinions?
This is the same as that!
phrases.notes: 'That' is the earlier case from steps 9 and 10: two say alive, one says dead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, using the explanation from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's line about two saying 'dead' and one saying 'not dead'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Repeating the same majority rule in a reverse case seems unnecessary.

steps.title: The majority counts even to be lenient
steps.stepSummary: The second case is needed. Without it, we might think the majority is followed only to be strict, not to permit her to marry.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: when we follow the majority, it is only to be strict, but not to be lenient. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the second case teaches something new about which direction the majority rule works in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first case used the majority to forbid her, which is strict. This case uses the majority to permit her to marry, which is lenient. The משנה shows that the majority rule works in both directions.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said: introduces a mistaken idea

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי נחמיה, the majority of opinions is followed both to forbid and to permit.

phrases.english: You might have said:
when we go after the majority of opinions,
it is to be strict,
but to be lenient, no;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a new point (strict compared to lenient)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The majority of opinions is followed only to be strict.
steps.terutzMaskana: The majority of opinions is followed to be lenient as well.

steps.title: One wife says he died, the other says he did not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that when two wives disagree about whether their husband died, the one who says he died may marry and collect her כתובה. The one who says he is alive may not marry and does not collect her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one wife says he died and the other says he did not, the one who says he died may remarry and collect her כתובה. The one who says he did not die may not remarry and does not collect her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It deals with two wives of the same man who give opposite reports about whether he died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each wife is judged by her own statement. The one who says he died is allowed to act on that, so she may remarry and collect. The one who says he is alive is held to her own words: she still counts herself as married, so she may not remarry, and she cannot collect her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה.
The marriage contract, which gives the wife money when the marriage ends.

steps.confusionAlert: The two wives get opposite results in the same case. This is not a contradiction. Each woman's own words decide what happens to her.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One wife says: "He died,"
and one says: "He did not die."
This one who says "He died"
may marry and takes her marriage contract money,
and this one who says "He did not die"
may not marry and does not take her marriage contract money.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״מֵת״ וְאַחַת אוֹמֶרֶת ״לֹא מֵת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the גמרא finished explaining the previous one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When two wives disagree, the one who says he died may remarry and collect her כתובה. The one who says he is alive may not remarry and does not collect.

steps.title: One wife says he died, the other says he was killed
steps.stepSummary: The wives disagree about how the husband died. רבי מאיר forbids both to marry because their stories contradict each other. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון allow both to marry because both agree he is dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one wife says he died and the other says he was killed, רבי מאיר says neither may marry, since they contradict each other. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון say both may marry, since both agree he is no longer alive.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings a second case. Here both wives say the husband is dead but disagree about how he died, and תנאים argue about the ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר looks at the disagreement. Since the two stories clash, he does not trust either one. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון look at what the two stories share: both agree the husband is dead, so the disagreement about how he died does not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: He was killed, meaning he died violently.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: a contradiction in the details ruins both statements. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון: if both agree on the main point, that the husband is dead, they may marry.

phrases.english: One says: "He died,"
and one says: "He was killed,"
Rabbi Meir says:
Since they contradict one another,
these women may not marry.
Rabbi Yehuda and Rabbi Shimon say:
Since both this one and that one agree
that he is not alive, they may marry.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case in the same משנה. Now both wives agree he is dead but disagree about how he died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: since they contradict each other, neither may marry. רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון: since both agree he is dead, both may marry.

steps.title: Start of a case where one witness contradicts another
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins a new case: one witness says the husband died and another witness says he did not. The ruling comes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: If one witness says he died and another witness says he did not die,
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is setting up its next case, two single witnesses who contradict each other. The ruling has not been given yet; it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה moves from wives contradicting each other to witnesses contradicting each other. Only the facts of the case appear here. The ruling comes next.

phrases.english: A witness says: "He died,"
and a witness says: "He did not die,"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the next case in the משנה, moving from wives who contradict each other to witnesses who contradict each other.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the case is stated here: one witness says the husband died and another says he did not. The ruling comes on the next amud.
